# psn_rom_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Rename PlayStation Network packages and license files to their content IDs.

## Synopsis

```
psn_rom_tool [options]
```

## Description

With `-r`, every PSN file under the input path is renamed in its own directory to the
36-character content ID it belongs to, such as
`UP0001-NPUB12345_00-GAMENAME00000001`:

- `.rap` files take the content ID from the `.pkg` file with the same base name next to
  them, so they are renamed before the packages are. A `.rap` without a matching
  `.pkg` is left alone.
- `.pkg` files take it from the package header.
- `.work.bin` and `.fake.rif` license files take it from their own contents.

Extensions are kept, so the results are `<content id>.rap`, `.pkg`, `.work.bin` and
`.fake.rif`.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | A PSN file, or a directory searched recursively for `.pkg`, `.rap`, `.work.bin` and `.fake.rif` files; must exist. |
| `-r, --rename` | Rename each file to `<content id>` plus its original extension. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Rename the PSN files in a folder

```bash
psn_rom_tool -i /path/to/psn -r
```

### Preview the renames without changing anything

```bash
psn_rom_tool -i /path/to/psn -r -p -v
```

## Notes

- A file whose new name is already taken is left as it is.
- Without `-r` nothing is done.
